templates.name: Proxmox Health Checkup
templates.description:
Check snapshots, non-vacuumed systemd unit files, old unpurged but not-in-use kernels, etc.

Image hygiene but for PVE nodes.

items.name: PVE - Snapshot Worst Severity (integer)
items.description:
Numeric worst severity across all VMs and LXC on this node.

0=OK
1=WARNING
2=HIGH
3=CRITICAL

Use this item in trigger expressions.

triggers.name: PVE - {HOST.NAME} CRITICAL snapshot state. Severity: {ITEM.LASTVALUE}
triggers.description:
One or more VMs or LXC containers on {HOST.NAME} is in a CRITICAL snapshot state.

This means: a snapshot >= 7 days old exists, OR multiple snapshots exist with at least one >= 5 days old.

Review /tmp/pve-snapshot-check.json on the host for the full list.

DO NOT auto-remove snapshots — check with a senior admin first.

Snapshots may be protecting an in-progress migration or backup job.

triggers.name: PVE - {HOST.NAME} HIGH snapshot state. Current value: {ITEM.LASTVALUE}
triggers.description:
One or more VMs or LXC containers on {HOST.NAME} has multiple snapshots.

Multiple snapshots consume significant disk space and can cause unexpected behaviour during live migration. Review /tmp/pve-snapshot-check.json on the host.

DO NOT auto-remove snapshots without authorisation.

triggers.name: PVE - {HOST.NAME} WARNING snapshot. Current value: {ITEM.LASTVALUE}
triggers.description:
One or more VMs or LXC containers on {HOST.NAME} has at least one snapshot.

Snapshots are not inherently a problem but forgotten ones consume disk space and can grow over time.

Review /tmp/pve-snapshot-check.json on the host.

items.name: /usr/local/bin/qm_type.sh script checksum
items.description:
/usr/local/bin/qm_type.sh allows text to be "typed" into a VM's console.

For example:

qm_type 112 'Welcome2026!'

would type Welcome2026! into the console of VM ID 112.

items.name: PVE - Backup Check Report (master)
items.description:
Reads the full JSON report written by pve-backup-check.py.

All other backup items depend on this master item. Script runs hourly; Zabbix polls hourly — any given poll reads the most recent run's output.

items.name: PVE - Snapshot Check Report (master)
items.description:

All other snapshot items depend on this master item. Script runs hourly; Zabbix polls hourly — any given poll reads the most recent run's output.

triggers.name: PVE - {HOST.NAME} backup check timer not enabled
triggers.description:
pve-backup-check.timer is not enabled.

Fix: systemctl enable --now pve-backup-check.timer + A stopped-but-enabled timer is caught by the backup report stale trigger.

items.name: PVE - Backup Check Report Exists
items.description: 1 = /tmp/pve-backup-check.json exists, 0 = missing. File is in /tmp so it is absent after a reboot until the timer next fires.

triggers.name: PVE - {HOST.NAME} backup report missing
triggers.description:
/tmp/pve-backup-check.json does not exist on {HOST.NAME}.

This is normal immediately after a reboot (file is in /tmp — volatile) and resolves once the timer fires (10 minutes after boot). If this persists beyond 15 minutes post-boot, investigate:

Check: systemctl status pve-backup-check.timer
Check: journalctl -u pve-backup-check.service -n 30
